title: APEX-7 Battery Cell Degradation
root_cause: Gradual capacity fade in Li-ion battery cell #3 due to thermal cycling fatigue after 18 months in LEO. Eclipse entry/exit temperature swings of 120°C accelerated SEI layer growth on the anode.
resolution: Load shedding of non-essential payload operations reduced bus draw by 4W. Adjusted charge cycle depth-of-discharge from 80% to 60% to reduce further degradation. Battery voltage stabilized within nominal range.
lessons_learned: Battery health monitoring algorithms should track coulombic efficiency per cell monthly. Thermal cycling models should inform battery replacement schedule proactively rather than reactively.
outcome: Mission continued with 15% reduced power budget. Primary objectives met.

title: TERRA-3 Solar Panel Thermal Excursion
root_cause: Off-nominal spacecraft attitude during eclipse exit exposed reverse side of Panel B to Earth infrared flux simultaneously with direct solar flux, causing 95°C peak temperature. The protective thermal coating had partially delaminated from a micrometeorite strike 6 months prior.
resolution: Attitude correction maneuver reoriented spacecraft within 12 minutes. Panel B was taken offline for thermal recovery. Redundant panel array maintained power positive margins. Attitude control parameters updated to prevent recurrence.
lessons_learned: Thermal coating integrity should be monitored via IR camera during annual inspection windows. Attitude control dead-bands should account for eclipse-exit geometry in high-beta angle seasons.
outcome: Full recovery within 48 hours. Panel B returned to service at 85% efficiency.

title: SOLARIS-2 Reaction Wheel Desaturation Attitude Anomaly
root_cause: Reaction wheel #2 reached saturation limit during a 4-hour ground contact gap. The autonomous desaturation routine failed to execute due to a software flag left in maintenance mode. Spacecraft drifted to 3.4-degree attitude error before ground commanded correction.
resolution: Ground-commanded precession maneuver using magnetic torquers restored nominal attitude in 22 minutes without propellant expenditure. Software maintenance mode flag added to pre-contact checklist.
lessons_learned: Software maintenance flags must be automatically cleared at contact end. Reaction wheel momentum budget monitoring should trigger autonomous alerts at 80% saturation rather than 100%.
outcome: No mission data loss. Zero fuel expenditure for recovery.

title: NEXUS-1 Propellant Feed Line Pressure Anomaly
root_cause: Micro-crack in propellant feed line thermal insulation caused a localized cold spot, elevating propellant viscosity and producing a transient 18 kPa pressure drop. Not a true propellant leak — the redundant pressure transducer confirmed nominal propellant mass.
resolution: Heater on feed line segment activated to normalize temperature. Pressure readings returned to nominal after 35 minutes. No propellant was lost. Mission continued without interruption.
lessons_learned: When a single pressure transducer shows anomalous readings, always cross-reference with redundant transducer and propellant mass balance before declaring a leak. Thermal blanket inspection should cover feed line segments.
outcome: False alarm. No propellant loss. Mission unaffected.

title: HYDRA-9 Communication Signal Degradation
root_cause: Primary S-band antenna gimbal motor stiction caused pointing loss of 2.3 degrees from ground station boresight. Signal dropped from -72 dBm to -104 dBm during critical data downlink window. Stiction was caused by outgassing lubricant re-condensation after a scheduled thruster firing.
resolution: Switched to backup omni antenna for critical housekeeping downlink. Antenna gimbal exercised through full range of motion to break stiction. Primary antenna recovered. Thruster firing schedule modified to avoid antenna pointing windows.
lessons_learned: High-value data downlink windows should not overlap with planned thruster operations. Antenna gimbal should be exercised weekly as part of routine operations to prevent stiction.
outcome: 12-minute data gap in science downlink. All critical housekeeping data retained.

title: CYGNUS-4 CPU Thermal Runaway
root_cause: An autonomous fault detection routine triggered a recursive loop consuming 94% of onboard CPU capacity, generating excess heat. The processor had no thermal throttling firmware at the installed version. CPU reached 71°C before the watchdog timer reset the processor.
resolution: Watchdog reset cleared the runaway process. Firmware updated to version 2.3.1 which includes hardware thermal throttling at 68°C. CPU load monitoring alert thresholds tightened from 90% to 75%.
lessons_learned: All autonomous software routines must include recursion depth limits and CPU budget governors. Thermal throttling should be implemented at firmware level independent of software.
outcome: Processor reset caused 3-minute safe-mode entry. No hardware damage.

title: ATLAS-5 Multi-Channel Power Bus Failure
root_cause: Primary power bus regulator failure caused voltage to drop to 19.2V, triggering under-voltage protection on three secondary buses simultaneously. The failure was traced to a component qualification deficiency — the regulator was rated for 3-year life but had operated for 4.2 years.
resolution: Spacecraft entered safe mode autonomously. Backup power bus activated. Regulator replaced in situ using pre-loaded contingency command sequence. Power nominal after 6 hours.
lessons_learned: Component lifetime tracking must account for actual mission extension beyond design life. Backup power bus should be exercised quarterly, not annually.
outcome: 6 hours of reduced operations. Full recovery to nominal. Mission extended 18 months.

title: MERIDIAN-2 Attitude Thruster Imbalance
root_cause: Thruster valve #4 failed to fully close after an orbit trim maneuver, producing a 0.3 N continuous thrust offset. Attitude error accumulated to 4.8 degrees over 90 minutes before ground detection. Continuous thruster leakage also caused fuel pressure decline of 8 kPa/hour.
resolution: Thruster #4 isolated via pyrotechnic cutoff valve. Attitude recovered using thrusters #1-3 asymmetric firing pattern. Fuel loss estimated at 2.1 kg. Mission replanned with reduced maneuver budget.
lessons_learned: Thruster valve closure confirmation should be mandatory telemetry check-item after every maneuver. Continuous attitude drift combined with fuel pressure decline is a diagnostic signature of thruster valve failure.
outcome: Mission objective met at 92% efficiency with reduced maneuver budget.

title: LIGHTHOUSE-3 Battery Voltage Drop in Eclipse
root_cause: New payload instrument activated for commissioning consumed 28W more than predicted in the power budget model. During eclipse, the battery discharge rate exceeded the designed 1C rate. Voltage dropped to 23.1V at deepest eclipse point.
resolution: Payload powered off immediately. Power budget model updated with measured consumption values. Battery recovered to nominal charge state within 2 orbits. Payload re-commissioned with corrected power schedule.
lessons_learned: New instrument commissioning must include measured power characterization before full operational activation. Eclipse power margin should be maintained at ≥20% of battery capacity.
outcome: Commissioning delayed by 5 days. No battery damage. Mission objectives met.

title: VEGA-7 Solar Array Drive Motor Anomaly
root_cause: Solar array drive assembly (SADA) motor experienced elevated friction torque at -40°C during a deep shadow eclipse, preventing array from tracking the sun during eclipse exit. Array was off-optimal angle by 23 degrees for 8 minutes after eclipse exit.
resolution: SADA heater activated to warm motor before eclipse entry per updated pre-contact procedure. Array tracking performance nominal after thermal soak. Power margin recovered within 2 orbits.
lessons_learned: SADA heaters should be activated 30 minutes before eclipse entry when spacecraft is in high-beta orbit seasons. Motor friction characterization should be part of annual health assessment.
outcome: Temporary power deficit resolved. No battery damage. Heater operations added 0.4W to power budget.

title: GEMINI-6 GPS Receiver Frequency Drift
root_cause: GPS receiver oscillator frequency drifted 4 Hz beyond specification due to long-term crystal aging. Position accuracy degraded from 5m to 85m CEP. Not a communication anomaly per se, but was detected via correlation with comm_signal_strength noise floor elevation.
resolution: Backup GPS receiver activated. Frequency calibration update uplinked to primary receiver. Primary receiver restored to specification. Oscillator replacement scheduled for next ground contact opportunity.
lessons_learned: GPS receiver oscillator aging should be monitored via periodic frequency calibration checks. Backup receiver should be kept warm (powered standby) rather than cold backup.
outcome: Position accuracy restored. Mission unaffected. Oscillator life model updated.

title: AURORA-1 Fuel Leak from Micro-Crack
root_cause: A micro-crack in a titanium propellant tank fitting, present since manufacturing but below detection threshold, propagated to 0.8mm under thermal cycling stress over 3.5 years. Propellant leak rate measured at 0.02 kg/day — sufficient to deplete mission-critical reserve within 18 months.
resolution: Propellant system isolated to healthy tank cluster. Leak source isolated to Tank #2. Mission replanned with reduced delta-V budget. Deorbit burn timeline accelerated by 8 months.
lessons_learned: Propellant tank fitting welds require higher-resolution X-ray inspection before flight. Tank pressure history logging at 1-hour intervals would have detected the anomaly 6 months earlier.
outcome: Mission completed successfully with 93% of science objectives met despite shortened mission timeline.

title: POLARIS-3 Star Tracker Thermal Cycling Failure
root_cause: Star tracker CCD detector developed a hot pixel cluster from accumulated total ionizing dose (TID) radiation over 5 years in MEO. Hot pixel contamination caused the centroiding algorithm to flag false stars, degrading attitude determination accuracy.
resolution: Star tracker software updated with hot pixel masking table generated from ground calibration analysis. Attitude determination accuracy restored to 2 arcseconds. Secondary star tracker maintained as primary for 30 days during calibration.
lessons_learned: Star tracker radiation performance should be modeled per orbit regime. Annual CCD calibration frames should be captured to track hot pixel growth rate.
outcome: Full attitude determination capability restored after 30 days. Mission extended.

title: DAWN-9 Reaction Control System Fuel Imbalance
root_cause: Asymmetric fuel usage across the redundant thruster branches caused 8% mass imbalance between the two propellant tanks, shifting the spacecraft center of mass by 2.3 cm. This manifested as a persistent 0.8-degree attitude offset requiring continuous correction torques.
resolution: Cross-feed valve opened to equalize fuel between branches. Attitude control gains adjusted to account for shifted center of mass. Fuel management procedure updated to balance tank usage within 5% throughout mission.
lessons_learned: Propellant mass balance between branches should be tracked at every ground contact and equalized proactively. Center of mass shift effects on attitude control should be modeled from day 1 of operations.
outcome: Mission performance restored. Estimated 1.2 kg propellant saved by eliminating continuous correction torques.

title: HORIZON-2 Comm System Uplink Interference
root_cause: Ground-based interference from an unauthorized Ka-band transmitter 340 km from the primary ground station introduced 6 dB additional noise into the uplink channel. The interference was geographically correlated with a new cellular infrastructure deployment.
resolution: Backup ground station activated for critical uplink contacts. Interference source identified and reported to national frequency regulatory authority. Primary ground station uplink frequency shifted by 4 MHz to avoid interference band.
lessons_learned: Ground station frequency coordination should include buffer margin to accommodate local RF environment changes. Uplink margin should be designed for 10 dB interference budget rather than 6 dB.
outcome: No mission data lost. Backup operations added 40 min/day of ground contact overhead.

title: TITAN-4 Battery Over-Temperature During Anomaly Response
root_cause: During a high-priority anomaly response mode, the onboard processor, battery charge controller, and solid-state recorder all ran simultaneously at 100% duty cycle, generating 12W more waste heat than predicted. Thermal model had not accounted for concurrent operation of all three subsystems.
resolution: Anomaly response mode power profile redesigned to sequence rather than parallelize high-power subsystems. Thermal margin restored. No hardware damage occurred as thermal limits were not breached, only approached.
lessons_learned: Thermal modeling must include worst-case simultaneous operating scenarios. Power and thermal engineers must jointly review all new operational modes before flight certification.
outcome: No hardware damage. Revised thermal model validated. Anomaly response capability maintained.

title: FALCON-8 Onboard Software Memory Corruption
root_cause: A single-event upset (SEU) from a high-energy galactic cosmic ray flipped a bit in the flight software command queue, causing the communication subsystem to interpret a housekeeping command as a power-off command for the transponder.
resolution: Hardware watchdog detected loss of transponder carrier and initiated autonomous reset sequence. Ground established contact 8 minutes later via backup transponder. Memory scrubbing algorithm activated. Primary transponder power-cycled successfully.
lessons_learned: All critical command queues must be protected with error-correcting code (ECC) memory. Autonomous watchdog reset procedures must be validated in hardware-in-the-loop testing before flight.
outcome: 8-minute communication outage. No data loss. ECC memory upgrade added to future missions.

title: MARS-RELAY-3 Solar Array Microfracture
root_cause: Three adjacent GaAs solar cells in Panel A developed microfractures from micrometeorite impact shrapnel, reducing that panel's power output by 11%. The fractures propagated slowly under thermal cycling, which is why the anomaly was not detected until 6 weeks after the impact event.
resolution: Power budget adjusted to account for reduced Panel A output. Remaining healthy cells in Panel A operated at higher voltage to partially compensate. No battery excursions observed with adjusted power profile.
lessons_learned: Solar panel current-voltage curve measurements should be taken weekly to detect gradual efficiency degradation. Micrometeorite flux models for mission trajectories should inform panel redundancy margins.
outcome: Mission continued at 97% of planned science objectives. Panel A remained in service at reduced efficiency.

title: OMEGA-5 Gyroscope Drift Accumulation
root_cause: Ring laser gyroscope #1 developed a slow bias drift of 0.003 deg/hour due to optical path degradation from UV radiation. The drift was within specification but at the upper tolerance boundary, causing attitude error to approach warning limits during extended maneuver sequences.
resolution: Gyroscope calibration sequence uploaded to null the bias. Star tracker-based attitude updates increased from hourly to every 15 minutes to limit drift accumulation. No change in mission operations required.
lessons_learned: Gyroscope bias parameters should be recalibrated every 3 months as part of routine maintenance. UV radiation contribution to optical path degradation in gyroscopes should be modeled per mission trajectory.
outcome: No mission impact. Calibration procedure added to routine operations schedule.

title: ECLIPSE-2 Eclipse Duration Prediction Error
root_cause: An updated ephemeris calculation revealed that the spacecraft's actual orbital precession rate differed from the planning model by 0.08 degrees/day, compounding over 6 months to produce a 14-minute longer eclipse than predicted. Battery was sized for maximum 38-minute eclipse; actual eclipse reached 52 minutes, causing deeper-than-designed discharge.
resolution: Power schedule adjusted to add 15-minute safe margin before eclipse. Battery depth-of-discharge reduced from 80% to 68%. Ephemeris update intervals tightened from monthly to weekly.
lessons_learned: Eclipse duration predictions must include orbital precession uncertainties with statistical confidence intervals. Battery sizing should use 95th percentile eclipse duration from Monte Carlo trajectory analysis.
outcome: Battery voltage floor stabilized. No capacity degradation detected after corrections.
